subject: Staged MAP: benchmarking velocity + unit-econ summary and close timeline
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Liz Carter <liz@finxlabs.com>, procurement@finxlabs.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged MAP: benchmarking velocity + unit-econ summary and close timeline

Liz — attaching the final MAP spreadsheet and a short executive summary of the throughput benchmarking we ran this week so you have everything for procurement and the engineering review. TL;DR: the sustained throughput target you asked for (250 QPS sustained with 512 token average per request) is achievable on our Dedicated profile with the tuned batching/kv-cache config; we measured TTFT and token throughput across two candidate variants.

Key benchmark highlights (summary):
- Test window: 2026-05-26 — 2026-05-29, region: us-west1 (GCP)
- Request profile: avg 512 tokens per request, 95th percentile request 1,100 tokens
- Sustained QPS achieved (steady-state 30+ minutes): 260 QPS (95% CI ±9) on rdw-dedicated.large with continuous batching and prefix cache
- Tokens/sec (model-level) sustained: 133k tokens/sec aggregate across serving pool (per-GPU peak ~22k tps)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) median: 68 ms; 95th: 145 ms (includes network + routing)
- Concurrency: validated up to 420 concurrent in-flight requests without backpressure; autoscaler held latency SLO via burst pool
- Unit economics (hosted vs. dedicated commit):
  • Hosted estimate: $0.72 per 1k tokens (on current hosted catalog variant)
  • Dedicated estimate (amortized HW + infra): $0.19 per 1k tokens at 1.2B tokens/day utilization (projected)

Attachments: finx_map_v2.xlsx (MAP milestones + acceptance criteria), throughput_plots.pdf (latency/throughput graphs), gcp_quote_20260530.pdf (pricing for the Dedicated pool sizing).

Proposed staged close timeline (condensed):
- 2026-06-03: procurement review completes (FinX)
- 2026-06-07: signature on 6-month Dedicated pilot (baseline commit)
- 2026-06-10 — 2026-06-24: deployment & traffic migration (canary -> 100%)
- 2026-07-01: performance acceptance (MAP acceptance: sustain 240 QPS for 48h, TTFT median < 80ms)

Next steps I propose: Marissa to confirm commercial point and DocuSign link, Rishi/Connor on a short pre-proc tech call w/ FinX eng to review tuning knobs (batching, KV cache TTLs, quant profile).

Grace

Thanks Grace — this is really helpful. A few quick clarifying questions before procurement signs: 

1) Can you confirm the model variant used for the peak tokens/sec numbers (is it a 34B commercial variant or a 16B open checkpoint)?
2) For the Dedicated estimate, what utilization assumptions drive the $0.19/1k tokens figure? We need a 6-month financial model for our CFO.
3) Any known constraints for our long-tail traffic spikes (we have unpredictable batch jobs overnight that can triple load for short windows).

Also want to schedule a tech sync with Rishi and Connor this week — procurement is fine gating signature on the answers above. 

— Liz

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged MAP: benchmarking velocity + unit-econ summary and close timeline

Liz — quick answers inline: 

1) Model variant: the reported numbers are for our "rdw-16b-quant" profile (16B open checkpoint, int8 quant with tuned kernels). We also ran short runs on a 34B float variant; tokens/sec dropped ~27% and TTFT rose ~60ms. If you prefer the larger model we can size differently.

2) Dedicated estimate assumptions: amortized GPU + infra over 12 months, 70% operational utilization during business hours, 40% overnight average; pricing assumes reserved instance commitments for 3 x A100-equivalent nodes. I'll attach the short cost sheet to the MAP (see finx_map_v2.xlsx). If you need a CFO-facing 6-month burn projection, Connor can produce a table with sensitivity to utilization.

3) Long-tail spikes: we recommend configuring burst capacity with a short-term autoscaler (adds ~1.5x capacity for up to 2 hours) + graceful fallback to smaller quantized variant. In our stress run we simulated 3x spikes for 20 minutes — latency rose to 310ms p95 but no request failures; tokens/sec scaled linearly until we hit per-GPU memory saturation.

Proposed tech sync times: Wed 2026-06-02 10:00 PT or Thu 2026-06-03 14:00 PT. Which works for you?

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Liz — thanks for the quick review and great questions. We had the tech sync earlier today (Connor + Rishi + FinX eng) and confirmed the following items to unblock procurement: 

Summary of today's confirmations (post-sync):
- Variant confirmed: rdw-16b-quant for pilot; optional 34B float as escalation path (cost delta ~+38%)
- Dedicated sizing for pilot: 3 nodes (A100-equivalent) with 1.5x burst pool available — expected steady-state sustain: 240–270 QPS depending on diurnal load
- Acceptance criteria for MAP (what FinX verifies in pilot):
  • Sustain >= 240 QPS for 48 continuous hours at avg 512 tokens/request
  • Median TTFT < 80 ms, p95 TTFT < 160 ms
  • No more than 0.1% failed requests over acceptance window
- Unit economics enclosed: pilot-level amortized cost $0.22 per 1k tokens at projected pilot utilization (conservative for CFO). Post-pilot scale targets reduce to ~$0.15 per 1k tokens.
- Procurement items: DocuSign link (Marissa) + SOW appendix for Dedicated throughput SLA (Grace to attach).

Action items: 
- Marissa: send DocuSign package and updated quote (today EOD).
- Connor: produce 6-month CFO table (sensitivity: utilization 40/60/80%) and upload to the Drive link.
- Liz/FinX: sign procurement checklist by 2026-06-03 to hit the proposed timeline.

I'll follow up once DocuSign is posted. Looking forward to closing the pilot and getting FinX live.
